vectors.description: an authorized governance key signed a checkpoint over registry version 5 and ledger entries 1 to 12; the supplied logs are exactly that state. Nothing says it is the latest, so it is unanchored
the same checkpoint against an anchor the caller already relies on that commits the same state
a checkpoint over registry version 1 and an empty ledger: zero entries committed, head null
one bit of the signature flipped
a valid signature by a key the trust root does not list: the signature is genuine and authorizes nothing
the statement names the root's key id but carries a different public key and is signed by that other key: a checkpoint cannot make itself trusted by naming a key
the registry being checkpointed lists this key as the WalletWall publication key; the registry cannot authorize the signer of its own checkpoint, only the trust root can
no governance trust root: nothing is authorized, and the verifier says it did not evaluate rather than defaulting
a trust root that is not itself valid (keys out of order) authorizes nothing
a key the trust root lists, authorized only for the deferred STANDING_HEAD purpose, signs a registry/ledger checkpoint
the supplied registry shares versions 1 to 4 with the committed one but its version 5 is a different valid history: the committed head is not in it
the supplied ledger has twelve valid entries but a different twelfth: its head is not the committed one
the supplied registry stops at version 4 although version 5 was committed
the supplied registry has a sixth version, and the caller asked for exactly the committed state: a different state is not this checkpoint
the supplied ledger stops at entry 11 although twelve were committed
the supplied ledger has a thirteenth entry, and the caller asked for exactly the committed state
a snapshot of the supplied registry was edited after publication without recomputing its digest: not a chain, so no comparison is made
an entry of the supplied ledger was edited after publication without recomputing its digest: not a ledger
a checkpoint over registry version 3 and a ledger whose last entry was accepted under version 4: both heads match, and the combination cannot have existed
an entry names registry version 2 with another registry's digest for it: the ledger prefix does not fit the committed registry
a checkpoint over registry version 4 and ledger entries 1 to 9, presented with a later state that extends it: valid, authorized, and silent about everything after its heads
the same old checkpoint, exactly its own state, when the caller already relies on the newer checkpoint of vector 01: authentic, and older than what is held
a checkpoint with the anchor's counts but a different registry head: not the state the caller relies on
a checkpoint ahead of the anchor on the registry and behind it on the ledger: logs only append, so no honest state is both

a checkpoint over registry version 6 and ledger entries 1 to 14, whose logs contain the anchored state and whose later entries name the registry heads that existed by then: it advances what the caller holds
a checkpoint over a later state, but of a different history than the anchor's: the anchored registry head is not in it
the committed registry and a ledger with one entry more than was committed, accepted as an extension: the extra entry is reported as uncovered
a registry with one version more than was committed, accepted as an extension: the extra version is reported as uncovered

checkpoint over registry 4 and ledger entries 1 to 12, signed while the key was ACTIVE; later versions record the key as compromised (retaining what was accepted before version 5). The genuine acceptance is entry 12, inside the checkpoint: its standing is held
the same checkpoint and logs: a statement the compromised key signed later, appended as entry 13 and naming registry version 4, lies after the authenticated prefix, so it keeps no standing

a later checkpoint over registry 6 and ledger entries 1 to 13, where entry 13 is the back-dated acceptance naming version 4, against an anchor whose registry head is 5: registry versions only grow, so an entry appended after that anchor cannot have been accepted under version 4. The checkpoint is refused as inconsistent, not authenticated

the same later checkpoint against an anchor taken while the registry head was still 4, before the compromise was recorded: entry 13 names version 4, which the anchor cannot show to be too old, so the checkpoint authenticates the ledger as it stands, including a back-dated entry. This is the stated residual: a checkpoint commits what governance signed over, it does not show each entry was rightly accepted
a signature over the checkpoint statement made under an attestation domain tag, presented as the checkpoint signature
a signature over the statement's JSON with no domain tag at all
the signature of a genuine assessor attestation presented as the checkpoint's signature
the committed registry head digest changed by one hex digit after signing
the committed ledger count changed from 12 to 13 after signing
a previous-checkpoint link smuggled into the statement: this version has no linkage, and an unknown field is refused, never dropped
the checkpoint was published under an identifier that is not the digest of its envelope
the identifier is exactly the digest of the envelope, recomputed by the reader
the signed twin of the version selector names a version this verifier does not read: refused as malformed, never reinterpreted
an envelope of a checkpoint version this verifier does not read
the statement names an algorithm this verifier does not support: not checked, never valid and never invalid
a signature of the wrong length
a public key of the wrong length inside the statement
S plus the group order: the same point equation, refused as non-canonical
a signature whose R is the identity point's encoding: refused as inadmissible before any platform check
a signature that is not lower-case hexadecimal is not a checkpoint
